sources.title: Meta Llama 3 model card
sources.evidence: Original Llama 3 pretrained and instruction-tuned variants: 8B and 70B nominal sizes, text input and text/code output, GQA, 8K context, and April 18, 2024 release. The card distinguishes base models from instruction-tuned models. Reopened for the October 27 parameter re-audit; the original card explicitly retains 70B parameters for the pretrained variant.

sources.title: Introducing Meta Llama 3: The most capable openly available LLM to date
sources.evidence: April 18, 2024 announcement releases pretrained and instruction-fine-tuned 8B/70B models, describes decoder-only Transformers and GQA, and specifies training on 8,192-token sequences. Longer context and multimodality are future goals for later releases.

sources.title: Llama 3 reference model implementation
sources.evidence: Transformer blocks invoke attention and one dense SwiGLU feed-forward network on every layer; there is no expert router. Model dimensions are supplied through ModelArgs, whose defaults alone do not identify the 70B checkpoint.

sources.title: Meta Llama 3 Community License Agreement
sources.evidence: The custom Meta Llama 3 license explicitly covers model weights and permits use, redistribution and modification subject to conditions. Its version release date is April 18, 2024.

sources.title: Original Meta Llama 3 repository README
sources.evidence: Documents released model weights, license-gated downloads, sequence support up to 8192 tokens for all original models, and pretrained models intended for text continuation rather than chat/Q&A fine-tuning. Later Llama 3.1 repository migration is identified separately.

sources.title: Meta-Llama-3-70B official base checkpoint
sources.evidence: Exact base repository is distinct from the Instruct variant and links Llama-3.1-70B as a newer model. Its usage examples target Meta-Llama-3-70B and its original checkpoints. The card contains an apparent copied 8B-Instruct sentence under How to use; that sentence is not used to identify this variant. Reopened for this parameter re-audit; the public card explicitly lists the original pretrained 70B parameter size.

sources.title: Meta-Llama-3-70B configuration access attempt
sources.evidence: Fresh unauthenticated request on October 27, 2026 again returned HTTP 401 requiring authorized access. No credentials, gate bypass, or weight downloads were attempted. This prevents an exact configuration-derived census but does not undermine Meta's published nominal 70B size.

sources.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models, Table 1
sources.evidence: The exact Llama 3 70B base row marks native tool use absent; original April models are distinguished from later Llama 3.1 and its instruction-tuned tool support.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V2 technical report, Table 2 and Figure 1(a)
sources.evidence: Freshly read May 7, 2024 version. Section 3.2.2 Table 2 explicitly lists LLaMA 3 70B with 70B in both the separate Activated Params and Total Params rows. It appears in the pre-training evaluation section; Section 4/Table 3 separately names the 70B Instruct model. Figure 1(a), visually inspected, corroborates approximately 70B on its Activated Parameters axis. The explicit table supplies nominal precision; this is DeepSeek's comparison convention, not a Meta active-count disclosure or an exact per-token tensor census.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V2 official repository, Base Model evaluation
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened official repository places LLaMA3 70B under Base Model / Standard Benchmark (Models larger than 67B). Its MMLU 78.9, BBH 81.0 and other scores match the Table 2 column, confirming the original pretrained comparator rather than the separately presented chat/instruct model.

sources.title: Meta current repository copy of the original Llama 3 model card
sources.evidence: Fresh search and reading of Meta's maintained repository copy confirms original Llama 3 pretrained and instruction-tuned variants at nominal 8B and 70B parameters, with April 18, 2024 release. It does not separately specify activated parameters or an exact learned count.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V2 June 19 revision, Table 2
sources.evidence: The later June 19, 2024 revision retains the original LLaMA 3 70B column with 70B Activated Params and 70B Total Params in Table 2, while Table 3 separately identifies 70B Inst. The later revision corroborates the nominal active convention; it provides no exact component participation census.

name.note: Original 70B pretrained base variant; official checkpoint identifier Meta-Llama-3-70B has no Instruct or 3.1 suffix.

developer.note: The original card identifies Meta as developer.

family.note: Catalog family key for original Llama 3, released before Llama 3.1.

release_date.note: Exact release day appears in the original card, dated announcement, and license.

open_weights.note: Meta released downloadable base weights under its custom license, with access approval; this is not a claim of an OSI-approved license.

license.note: Existing label denotes the custom Meta Llama 3 Community License Agreement.

parameters_b.note: Freshly reopened original announcement, original card, exact base checkpoint and current repository card all support Meta's nominal 70B total. This is a published model size, not an exact tensor census; configuration access remains gated, and no weight shards were downloaded.

active_parameters_b.note: DeepSeek-V2 Table 2 explicitly reports 70B Activated Params for original LLaMA 3 70B. The official repository labels the matching benchmark column Base Model, and the paper treats 70B Instruct separately. Adopt 70B as DeepSeek-AI's nominal comparison convention, corroborated by the later paper revision and Figure 1(a), rather than infer active from dense architecture. Exact component scope and per-token participation are not established by this convention.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only Transformer with grouped-query attention. The official implementation executes one feed-forward network per block without expert routing; model-parallel layers do not imply mixture-of-experts.

context_window.note: The original README explicitly supports sequences up to 8192 tokens; the announcement states the same sequence length. Later 3.1 context specifications do not apply.

modalities.note: Official inputs are text and outputs text/code; code is represented as text. No original base-model image or audio modality is documented.

reasoning.note: General reasoning benchmarks and improved reasoning claims do not establish a dedicated native reasoning mode for this base checkpoint; no such mode is documented in the examined original sources.

tool_call.note: Meta explicitly marks native tool use absent for the original Llama 3 70B base model in Table 1. External prompting and downstream fine-tunes do not change that released native capability.

description.value: Original Llama 3 70B pretrained text-generation model with a dense decoder-only Transformer, grouped-query attention, and an 8,192-token context.
description.note: Makes the original base variant explicit and restricts claims to documented architecture and context.

patch.description: Original Llama 3 70B pretrained text-generation model with a dense decoder-only Transformer, grouped-query attention, and an 8,192-token context.
patch.notes: 70B total is Meta's nominal size; 70B active follows DeepSeek-V2 Table 2's published comparison convention. Neither is an exact tensor or per-token census. Original April 2024 base checkpoint with 8192-token context, distinct from Llama 3.1. A dedicated reasoning mode is not documented; Meta marks native tool use absent.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retained Meta's nominal 70B total and resolved active parameters to 70B using the explicit original LLaMA 3 70B column in DeepSeek-V2 Table 2. DeepSeek's official Base Model comparison confirms variant identity; the later June paper revision retains the count, and Figure 1(a) visually corroborates it. Fresh original and migrated Meta cards and announcement still support 70B total. The active value follows DeepSeek-AI's published benchmark convention, not a separate Meta disclosure or an exact per-token census. A fresh official configuration request still returns HTTP 401; no shards were downloaded. The twelve nonparameter assessments are preserved.
